title: CloudWatch Logs & Alarms 🚨
description: Centralize logs, create metric filters, and set up alarms that trigger automated actions.

slides.title: CloudWatch Logs: A Single Pane for Logs 📝
slides.content:
# Aggregate Everything

CloudWatch Logs lets you store, monitor, and access log files from:
- EC2 instances (via CloudWatch agent)
- Lambda functions (automatically)
- RDS databases
- VPC Flow Logs
- CloudTrail
- Any application using the PutLogEvents API

**Log groups** are containers for log streams. A **log stream** is a sequence of log events from the same source (e.g., one Lambda function, one EC2 instance).

quizData.question: In CloudWatch Logs, what is the relationship between log groups and log streams?

options.text: A log group contains one log stream
A log stream contains multiple log groups
A log group can contain many log streams, each representing a source

quizData.explanation: Think of a log group as a folder, and log streams as files inside that folder. Each stream holds events from a specific source (e.g., instance i-123).

slides.title: Metric Filters: Turn Logs into Metrics 🔍
slides.content:
# Extract Meaning from Text

You can create **metric filters** on log groups to search for specific patterns (e.g., "ERROR", "404") and increment a custom metric each time it appears.

**Example**: Your application logs "Payment failed" messages. Create a metric filter for that string, and a CloudWatch metric `Payments/Failures` will track how many times it occurs. Then you can set an alarm on that metric!

This transforms qualitative log data into actionable quantitative data.

slides.title: CloudWatch Alarms: The Watchdog 🐕
slides.content:
# Act Before It's Too Late

An **alarm** monitors a metric over a time period and performs one or more actions when the threshold is breached.

- Choose a metric (e.g., `CPUUtilization`).
- Set a condition (e.g., greater than 80% for 5 consecutive minutes).
- Define actions: send an SNS notification, auto‑scale an EC2 instance, stop/terminate an instance, trigger a Lambda function.

Alarm states: **OK** (metric within threshold), **ALARM** (threshold breached), **INSUFFICIENT_DATA** (not enough data to judge).

quizData.question: Which AWS service is commonly used to send an email when a CloudWatch alarm is triggered?
quizData.explanation: SNS (Simple Notification Service) topics are the standard way to fan out notifications, including to email and SMS.

slides.title: Composite Alarms: Combine Signals 🧩
slides.content:
# Reduce Noise

A composite alarm watches multiple other alarms using a boolean expression (AND/OR). You might have:
- Alarm A: CPU > 80%
- Alarm B: Memory > 90%
- Composite: A AND B → triggers only when both are in alarm.

This avoids alert fatigue. Only fire when the situation is truly critical.

slides.title: Dashboards: The Visual Command Center 📊
slides.content:
# Single Pane of Glass

CloudWatch Dashboards let you create custom, real‑time visualisations of your metrics. You can add:
- Line graphs, stacked area, number widgets
- Metrics from multiple regions and accounts (cross‑account)
- Log query results

Dashboards are perfect for NOC screens, team status pages, or quick health checks. They auto‑refresh and can be shared.

slides.title: Pro Tip: Anomaly Detection 🚀
slides.content:
## Smart Alarms

CloudWatch supports anomaly detection on metrics. Instead of static thresholds, it learns the normal pattern and alarms when the metric deviates significantly. Ideal for seasonal traffic.
